$comment: Small extracts for examples and scenarios: heritage of a few countries from national-strengths/build/heritage-all.json (authored merged over generated), trimmed catalogue records (only the fields archetype generation reads) from country-catalogue/build/catalogue.json, and the event links they use.

birthright.name: Sagres pilots
birthright.text: Ships build 15 % faster, storms sink a third fewer, sea crossings take 10 % fewer days; ports raise 20 % more sailors and fisheries feed 20 % more.
birthright.why: Under Prince Henry, pilots from Lagos near Sagres charted Madeira, the Azores and the coast past Bojador (1434) and Arguin (1443); the kingdom lived from fishing, salt and the sea.

heydays.name: Carreira da Índia
heydays.text: Traders on sea routes gather 30 % more; harbours cost a quarter less; customs officers on the coast are 20 % stronger.
heydays.why: The catalogue's 'route to India' path: the Cape rounded in 1488 and India reached in 1498, after which Lisbon's crown fleets ran the yearly India voyage.

mark.name: Cape charts
mark.text: Sea crossings take 10 % fewer days and sea traders gather 5 % more.

heydays.name: Engenhos of Brazil
heydays.text: Sugar output +30 %, plantations cost a quarter less, ports offer 20 % more seafolk jobs, and the coast grows 10 % faster.
heydays.why: Madeira sugar (from the 1440s) was the model for the Brazilian captaincies and engenhos of the 1500s; inferred from the catalogue's Atlantic-island economy.

heydays.name: Gold of the Gerais
heydays.text: Gold output +40 %, loans cost 20 % less interest, and masters of works are 20 % stronger.
heydays.why: The Brazilian gold strikes of the 1690s financed Lisbon's court and building programme into the 1750s (inferred from the catalogue's Atlantic path).

burden.name: Bread from abroad
burden.text: Harvests roll one step worse and people grow 5 % slower.
burden.why: The catalogue lists a small population and a grain deficit as Portugal's constraints; the kingdom bought wheat from abroad and from Madeira.
burden.shed_text: Learn Maize, potato and cassava, or build 5 more granaries than you began with.

turned.name: Island wheat
turned.text: Stores rot 30 % less; coastal harvests roll one step better; fisheries feed 20 % more.

ambitions.name: Beyond the Cape of Storms
ambitions.hint: Where the storms guard the turning of the world.
ambitions.text: Hold Goa or Calicut on the Malabar coast.

legacy.name: Estado da Índia
legacy.text: One more trader; customs officers on the coast 20 % stronger; carracks hit 15 % harder; sea traders gather 5 % more.

ambitions.name: The gold of Mina
ambitions.hint: Past the river of gold, a castle on the shore.
ambitions.text: Hold Elmina on the Gold Coast.

legacy.name: Casa da Mina
legacy.text: Gold output +25 %; tax reaching you from the coast +10 %.

ambitions.name: Over the Strait
ambitions.hint: Ceuta was the first stone; the wall needs three more.
ambitions.text: Hold Ceuta, Tangier and Arzila in Morocco.

legacy.name: Praças de África
legacy.text: Garrisons 20 % stronger; commanders may fight à la jineta.

ambitions.name: Crown of the two seas
ambitions.hint: Aljubarrota's victors may yet sit in Toledo.
ambitions.text: Join Castile to the Portuguese crown in personal union, with Lisbon still independent.

legacy.name: Lisbon and Toledo
legacy.text: Two more lords can be kept without strain; Latin-group subjects take your tongue 30 % faster.

ambitions.name: Land of the True Cross
ambitions.hint: A red wood on a western shore no one meant to find.
ambitions.text: Hold eight colonies or posts in Brazil.

legacy.name: The captaincies
legacy.text: Coast grows 10 % faster, sugar output +15 %, and 20 % more fleeing farmers choose you.

ambitions.name: The acclamation
ambitions.hint: Sixty years under another's crown, then a balcony in Lisbon.
ambitions.text: After a union with Spain, win independence again and keep it.

legacy.name: House of Braganza
legacy.text: Foreign bribes no longer sway your lords; your homeland resists conquerors 30 % longer.

birthright.name: Lagoon and Arsenal
birthright.text: Galleys build 30 % faster, the capital's garrison is 40 % stronger, and ports raise 15 % more sailors.
birthright.why: The Arsenal was the state shipyard producing galleys, and the catalogue notes that the lagoon made the capital nearly impregnable.

heydays.name: The mude to Alexandria
heydays.text: Sea traders gather 25 % more and customs officers are 30 % stronger.
heydays.why: State galley convoys (mude) sailed to Alexandria, Beirut, Constantinople, Flanders and England, giving Venice the spice trade.

heydays.name: Aldine presses
heydays.text: Book output +40 % and presses cost a quarter less.
heydays.why: Inferred: Venice's capital, paper trade and scholars from Padua made it Europe's largest printing centre around 1500.

heydays.name: Morosini's galleys
heydays.text: At war with the Ottomans: galleys hit 20 % harder, sieges 15 % faster, prizes and ransoms bring 30 % more gold.
heydays.why: Inferred from the catalogue's Ottoman-Venetian war path: Venice fought the Ottomans for its Levant holdings for two centuries.

burden.name: The feared lion
burden.text: Each province you seize counts 25 % more toward Lands taken, and hired companies cost 20 % more.
burden.why: The catalogue lists coalitions fearing Venetian hegemony and dependence on mercenary commanders as Venice's constraints.
burden.shed_text: Have at least 3 allies and stability of at least 2.

turned.name: The Serene Republic
turned.text: Broken oaths fade 30 % faster; neighbours think one step better of you.

ambitions.name: Queen Caterina's gift
ambitions.hint: A patrician's daughter marries a king of an island of sugar.
ambitions.text: Hold Cyprus.

legacy.name: Kingdom of Cyprus
legacy.text: Sugar output +20 %; trade profit on Cyprus +40 %.

ambitions.name: A lion on the Adda
ambitions.hint: The Visconti line is ending; the river is a border only by habit.
ambitions.text: Hold Bergamo, Brescia and Crema.

legacy.name: Provveditori in the field
legacy.text: Wardens 30 % stronger; garrisons 10 % stronger.

ambitions.name: The doge's oldest debt
ambitions.hint: Chioggia was a lifetime ago, but the lagoon remembers.
ambitions.text: Make Genoa your subject, or see it gone from the map.

legacy.name: Queen of the seas
legacy.text: One more trader, ships hit 15 % harder, ports raise 10 % more sailors, and sea crossings take 10 % fewer days.

ambitions.name: Kingdom of the Morea
ambitions.hint: Coron and Modon were the eyes of the Republic.
ambitions.text: Own the Morea.

legacy.name: Morean fortresses
legacy.text: Each castle feeds one more ring of provinces; Foreign rule fades 20 % faster.

ambitions.name: Pepper by another road
ambitions.hint: Portuguese sails round Africa; the Senate looks at a map of Suez.
ambitions.text: Hold a fifth of the trade power in the Red Sea.

legacy.name: Cut at Suez
legacy.text: Sea traders gather 10 % more, sea crossings 10 % shorter, and 20 % more traders pass your coast.

ambitions.name: After Cambrai
ambitions.hint: Pope, emperor and king have signed a league to share you.
ambitions.text: Be independent in 1520 or later, owning half of Lombardy and the Veneto.

legacy.name: Cernide
legacy.text: Recruits refill 15 % faster; your homeland resists conquerors 30 % longer.

birthright.name: Nzimbu shell money
birthright.text: Tax reaching you +15 %, tribute +30 %, and raffia cloth output +20 %.
birthright.why: The king's governors collected tribute in raffia cloth, food and nzimbu shells from Luanda island (royal control attested from the 16th century, probably older).

heydays.name: Afonso's church
heydays.text: School seats +30 %, faith spreads 25 % faster, one more envoy, legitimacy +5.
heydays.why: Nzinga a Nkuwu was baptised in 1491 and Afonso I built a Kongolese Catholic church, schools and embassies to Lisbon and Rome (event-tree kongo_christianization).

heydays.name: Garcia II's Dutch league
heydays.text: Musketeers hit 25 % harder, homeland resists conquerors 30 % longer, sea traders gather 15 % more.
heydays.why: The catalogue's adaptation is to seek an alliance with a maritime partner; in the 1640s Kongo allied with the Dutch against Portuguese Luanda (inferred from regional history).

burden.name: Contested succession
burden.text: Lords start one step less loyal, and legitimacy -10.
burden.why: Kingship passed among descendants of the founder chosen by electors; the catalogue lists contested successions as the first constraint and succession civil war as a failure condition.
burden.shed_text: Have 2 more loyal lords than you began with, no noble revolt, and learn Written law codes.

turned.name: Settled succession
turned.text: A new ruler or a disputed heir no longer lowers lords' loyalty.

ambitions.name: Strangers from the sea
ambitions.hint: White sails at the mouth of the Nzadi bring gifts and a new god.
ambitions.text: Ally with Portugal.

legacy.name: São Salvador
legacy.text: Legitimacy +10; Catholic lands think one step better of you.

ambitions.name: Lord of the Mbundu
ambitions.hint: South of the Dande the chiefs pay when they must.
ambitions.text: Hold half of northern Angola.

legacy.name: Mbundu tribute
legacy.text: Tribute +25 %; seized land alarms 15 % less.

ambitions.name: Masters of the Pool
ambitions.hint: Where the great river widens into a lake, the Tio take the tolls.
ambitions.text: Make the Tio your subject, or end them.

legacy.name: Canoes of the Pool
legacy.text: River traders gather 20 % more; copper output +10 %.

ambitions.name: Mbwila never comes
ambitions.hint: The governor in Luanda counts his soldiers and your provinces.
ambitions.text: Hold Mbanza Kongo, independent, in 1680.

legacy.name: The kingdom unbroken
legacy.text: Homeland resists 40 % longer; lost wars no longer shake lords; garrisons +15 %.

ambitions.name: The island of shells
ambitions.hint: Our money grows on an island; strangers want to build a fort there.
ambitions.text: Own Luanda in 1600.

legacy.name: Royal shell fishery
legacy.text: Tax reaching you +10 %; fisheries +20 %; trade profit +5 %.

ambitions.name: Return to Vungu
ambitions.hint: The founder crossed the river from the north; his heirs could cross back.
ambitions.text: Make Loango and Kakongo your subjects.

legacy.name: House of both banks
legacy.text: Bantu lands think one step better of you; sea traders gather 10 % more.

ambitions.name: Royal schools
ambitions.hint: Noble sons learn letters, and letters reach Lisbon and Rome.
ambitions.text: Keep 3 schools.

legacy.name: Lettered nobility
legacy.text: Schoolmasters +30 %; +1 official supported.

birthright.name: Salt of Wieliczka, grain of the Vistula
birthright.why: The royal salt mines of Wieliczka and Bochnia were a main source of crown revenue, and Poland's farmland fed a growing grain export down the Vistula.

heydays.name: Rafts to Danzig
heydays.text: River traders gather a quarter more, granaries cost 30 % less, and farmers' job slots +15 %.
heydays.why: The catalogue names the Vistula grain and timber route to Danzig as Poland's chief trade, held back only by the Order's control of the river mouth.

heydays.name: A state without stakes
heydays.text: Wrong faith angers no province, 40 % more fleeing scholars choose you, and schools seat a quarter more.
heydays.why: Inferred: the 16th-century noble republic guaranteed peace between faiths, building on the catalogue's protected Jewish, Armenian and Orthodox communities and the Kraków university.

heydays.name: Winged hussars
heydays.text: Commanders may lead the hussar charge, lancers hold 10 points longer, horses bred +25 %.
heydays.why: Inferred from the catalogue's mass noble cavalry: in the 17th century the Commonwealth's hussars were its decisive arm (Kircholm, Vienna 1683).

burden.name: The elected crown
burden.text: Nothing is granted without the nobles: a tenth of taxes never arrives, and levies serve two months less before pay is due.
burden.why: The catalogue names noble consent for taxes and war as Poland's main constraint; the levy was reluctant to serve abroad.
burden.shed_text: Learn Written constitution while staying independent.

turned.name: Government law
turned.text: A tenth more tax reaches you and half a point more troop cap share.

ambitions.name: One king for Kraków and Vilnius
ambitions.hint: The brother sits in Vilnius; the throne in Kraków is empty.
ambitions.text: Rule Lithuania in personal union.

legacy.name: House of Jagiełło
legacy.text: A new ruler no longer costs lords' loyalty, and one more envoy.

ambitions.name: The river's mouth
ambitions.hint: The grain is ours; the harbour is theirs.
ambitions.text: Hold Danzig and Marienburg.

legacy.name: Royal Prussia
legacy.text: Customs officers 30 % stronger, one more trader, tolls +10 %.

ambitions.name: One commonwealth
ambitions.hint: Two crowns, one sejm, one coin.
ambitions.text: Bind Lithuania into one commonwealth, or hold most of its lands.

legacy.name: Sejm of two nations
legacy.text: Two more lords before strain, and Foreign rule fades a quarter faster.

ambitions.name: A port on the Black Sea
ambitions.hint: From Lwów the road runs down to Akkerman.
ambitions.text: Hold Lwów and a harbour on the Black Sea.

legacy.name: Road to Akkerman
legacy.text: Sea traders gather 15 % more and 15 % more traders pass your lands.

ambitions.name: Crowns of the house
ambitions.hint: Three thrones south of the mountains want a Jagiellon.
ambitions.text: Rule Bohemia and Hungary in personal union.

legacy.name: Crowns of the house
legacy.text: Prestige +1 and countries of your faith one step friendlier.

ambitions.name: The sun stands still
ambitions.hint: A canon of Frombork moves the earth.
ambitions.text: Know Observatories and have at least ten scholars.

legacy.name: Revolutions of the spheres
legacy.text: Observatories, ocean navigation and the chronometer cost a fifth less; schools seat 10 % more.

birthright.name: Mesta and jinetes
birthright.text: Herds grow 25 % faster and wool output is 25 % higher; commanders may fight à la jineta.
birthright.why: Transhumant Mesta flocks and merino wool via Burgos were Castile's wealth, and the Granadan frontier bred light cavalry (jinetes) that won La Higueruela in 1431.

heydays.name: The war of Granada
heydays.text: While fighting Granada: sieges 20 % faster, bombards hit 10 % harder, armies forage 20 % more, levies serve 2 months free.
heydays.why: The catalogue's conquest-of-Granada path: a ten-year war of sieges and frontier raids (1482-1492) fought with royal artillery and town levies.

heydays.name: Tercios
heydays.text: Commanders may form tercios; standing regiments break 10 points later; recruits refill 10 % faster; hired companies cost 10 % less.
heydays.why: Inferred: the Castilian infantry that grew from the Granada and Italian wars dominated European battlefields in the 1500s.

heydays.name: Casa de Contratación
heydays.text: Silver output +30 %, customs officers 30 % stronger, and storms sink a fifth fewer ships.
heydays.why: The catalogue's Atlantic path: Seville became the licensed port of the Indies trade, with silver fleets sailing in convoy.

burden.name: Kings and favourites
burden.text: Lords start one step less loyal, the court supports one lord fewer, and lords' lands send 10 % less tax.
burden.why: In 1444 the king was a prize fought over by Álvaro de Luna, the Infantes of Aragon and noble leagues, and crown revenue had been granted away to magnates.
burden.shed_text: Keep at least 6 loyal lords and stability of at least 2.

turned.name: Royal corregidores
turned.text: Seized land no longer angers your lords; officials cost 10 % less; one more official without strain.

ambitions.name: The pomegranate
ambitions.hint: The last fruit of the long reconquest hangs ripe in the south.
ambitions.text: Own the area of Granada.

legacy.name: Keys of the Alhambra
legacy.text: Granada changes faith 50 % faster; clergy lords start one step more loyal; garrisons 10 % stronger.

ambitions.name: Tanto monta
ambitions.hint: A bride, a groom and two crowns that weigh the same.
ambitions.text: Bind Aragon to your crown in a personal union.

legacy.name: The Catholic Monarchs
legacy.text: Two more lords without strain; Foreign rule fades 25 % faster.

ambitions.name: Beyond Hierro
ambitions.hint: West of the last island, the sea has another shore.
ambitions.text: Hold six colonies or posts in the Americas.

legacy.name: Council of the Indies
legacy.text: One more trader; stewards 30 % stronger; Foreign rule fades 10 % faster.

ambitions.name: Hispania whole
ambitions.hint: Aljubarrota's debt can be repaid with a wedding.
ambitions.text: Hold Portugal in personal union under your crown.

legacy.name: One peninsula
legacy.text: Coastal trade profit +10 %, ports raise 20 % more sailors, and seizures alarm neighbours 15 % less.

ambitions.name: Santa Hermandad
ambitions.hint: Bandits on the roads, a brotherhood with bows.
ambitions.text: Triple your officials and hold stability at +1 or better.

legacy.name: Brotherhood of the roads
legacy.text: Wardens are 40 % stronger.

ambitions.name: Wool for Bruges
ambitions.hint: The fleece goes north from Burgos; let the gold come back.
ambitions.text: Keep a trade pact with Burgundy and field four traders.

legacy.name: Consulado of Burgos
legacy.text: Sea traders gather 15 % more; tolls bring 20 % more gold.

birthright.name: Consulate of the Sea
birthright.text: Sea traders gather 20 % more, galleys build 20 % faster, and loans cost a quarter less interest.
birthright.why: Barcelona's and Valencia's sea trade ran under the Consolat de Mar, Catalan galleys sailed to Sicily and the Levant, and Valencian censals made the Crown's credit cheap.

heydays.name: The Magnanimous
heydays.text: While Naples is yours: galleys hit 20 % harder, sieges 15 % faster, and one more envoy.
heydays.why: Alfonso V conquered Naples in 1442, kept his court and fleet there and ran the Crown's Italian diplomacy from it.

heydays.name: Valencia's golden century
heydays.text: Pottery output +40 %, Valencia's trade profit +40 %, and loans cost 20 % less interest.
heydays.why: The catalogue calls Valencia a booming port and financial centre, the source of loans to Alfonso, famous for Manises ceramics.

burden.name: Pactist Corts
burden.text: Tax reaching you -10 %; levies serve one month less before pay; one official fewer without strain.
burden.why: Each realm's Corts voted taxes and could refuse them, and the king lived in Naples; the catalogue lists pactist estates and an absent king as constraints.
burden.shed_text: Learn Professional bureaucracy and reach stability of at least 2.

turned.name: Generalitat's credit
turned.text: Loans cost 30 % less interest; tax reaching you +5 %; tax collectors 10 % stronger.

ambitions.name: The kingdom across the sea
ambitions.hint: A crown won at Ponza's price must not pass to a bastard line.
ambitions.text: Own the area of Naples, or hold Naples as your subject or in union.

legacy.name: Regia Camera della Sommaria
legacy.text: Subjects send 25 % more tribute; tax collectors 20 % stronger.

ambitions.name: The heir's marriage

legacy.name: Two crowns, one court
legacy.text: One more envoy, one more lord without strain, and Castile's opinion of you one step better.

ambitions.name: The Roussillon road

ambitions.text: Hold Perpignan in 1500 or later.

legacy.name: Salses wall

ambitions.name: Corsica's old claim

legacy.name: Masters of the Tyrrhenian

legacy.name: Sentence of Guadalupe

ambitions.hint: Pepper still comes to Barcelona, if Venice would only let it.

legacy.name: Catalan consuls

birthright.text: Conquerors' Foreign rule lasts 55 % longer here; garrisons 40 % stronger; fisheries feed 30 % more.
birthright.why: Byzantine Empire's core lay on islands: the sea was its wall and its larder.

birthright.why: Hungary was Europe's leading gold producer, raised its armies from the banderia of barons and prelates, and had extensive grazing for horses and cattle.

heydays.name: Hunyadi's captains
heydays.text: Commanders may fight as hussar raiders; garrisons +25 %, hired companies cost a quarter less, sieges 10 % faster.
heydays.why: The catalogue's Hungary fights aggressive frontier wars under capable captains like Hunyadi and hires Hussite-trained companies; the paid army under Matthias is inferred.

heydays.name: Mills of Pest
heydays.text: Grain output +40 %, mills cost 30 % less and rail stations 10 % less.
heydays.why: Inferred: the fertile plains and Danube trade in the catalogue made Buda-Pest a great milling centre once railways came.

burden.name: Barons' leagues
burden.text: A tenth of taxes stays with the barons who hold royal pledges, and lords start one step less loyal.
burden.why: The catalogue lists baronial fragmentation and limited royal revenue, much of it pledged or seized during the civil war, as Hungary's constraints.

ambitions.name: The crown comes home
ambitions.hint: A queen's maid carried it off in a cushion.
ambitions.text: Hold Székesfehérvár, be independent and have at least five loyal lords.

legacy.name: Doctrine of the Holy Crown
legacy.text: Legitimacy +10, and a disputed heir no longer costs lords' loyalty.

ambitions.name: The raven in Vienna
ambitions.hint: The emperor's city has walls, but no money for its soldiers.
ambitions.text: Hold Vienna.

legacy.name: Raven over the Hofburg
legacy.text: New land alarms neighbours a fifth less and Foreign rule fades a quarter faster.

ambitions.name: A library of kings
ambitions.hint: Florentine scribes copy for a Danube king.
ambitions.text: Have at least eight scholars and two presses.

legacy.name: Bibliotheca Corviniana
legacy.text: Scholars research 10 % more and 30 % more fleeing scholars choose you.

ambitions.name: Banates to the sea
ambitions.hint: Wallachia, Serbia and Bosnia, three shields before the crown.
ambitions.text: Have at least three subjects, Wallachia and Serbia among them.

legacy.name: Southern banates
legacy.text: Tribute +30 %, tolls +20 % and horses bred +10 %.

birthright.name: Herds of Wallachia
birthright.text: Herds grow 40 % faster, herder slots +30 %, armies forage 30 % more.
birthright.why: Wallachia's wealth was counted in animals.

heydays.name: Cattle wealth
heydays.text: Herds grow 40 % faster, horses 30 % faster, recruits refill 25 % faster.
heydays.why: Inferred: herding peoples grew strong in good grazing years.

burden.name: Drought years
burden.text: Herds grow 20 % slower and people 5 % slower.

turned.name: Wells and grazing law
turned.text: Herds grow 25 % faster and stores rot 25 % less.

ambitions.name: Outlast Ottoman Empire
ambitions.hint: An old enemy at the gate.
ambitions.text: See Ottoman Empire fall, or make it your subject.

legacy.name: Marcher lords
legacy.text: Each province taken counts 20 % less toward Lands taken; conquered land settles 25 % faster.

ambitions.name: Take Suceava
ambitions.hint: A rival's hearth.
ambitions.text: Hold Suceava, the seat of Moldavia.

legacy.name: Veteran captains
legacy.text: New commanders start with one more Might; break point +5 points.

ambitions.name: One crown with Hungary
ambitions.hint: A friend who could be family.
ambitions.text: Bring Hungary under your crown, as a subject or in a union.

legacy.name: Loyal houses
legacy.text: Lords start a step more loyal; retinues 20 % larger.

ambitions.name: A full treasury
ambitions.hint: Coin that counts itself.
ambitions.text: Hold five times the gold you began with and owe nothing.

legacy.name: Thrifty court
legacy.text: Officials cost 15 % less; buildings cost 20 % less.

ambitions.name: Endure
ambitions.hint: Still standing when the world has changed.
ambitions.text: Be independent in 1600.

legacy.name: Unbowed
legacy.text: Conquerors' Foreign rule lasts 40 % longer; garrisons 15 % stronger.

birthright.name: Erzberg iron, Vienna staple
birthright.text: Iron output +30 %, salt output +20 %, and Vienna's trade profit +40 %.
birthright.why: The catalogue names the Styrian Erzberg iron trade, salt at Aussee and Hallstatt, and Vienna's Danube staple right as Austria's resources.

heydays.name: Marriages, not wars
heydays.text: One more envoy, countries of your faith one step friendlier, Foreign rule fades 30 % faster, legitimacy +5.
heydays.why: The catalogue's Austria expands through inheritance treaties, guardianships and marriages rather than conquest.

heydays.name: The border against the crescent
heydays.text: Garrisons 30 % stronger, castles cost 30 % less, and quartered soldiers no longer anger the frontier.
heydays.why: The catalogue records Ottoman raids into Carniola and Styria and a path of repeated raids from the 1470s; Mohács (1526) brought the frontier to Austria.

heydays.name: After the second siege
heydays.text: New land alarms neighbours a quarter less, Foreign rule fades 30 % faster, standing regiments hold 10 points longer.
heydays.why: Inferred from the event tree: after the siege of Vienna in 1683 the Habsburgs reconquered Hungary up to the Treaty of Karlowitz.

burden.name: Pledged domains
burden.text: Debt interest 40 % higher, and 8 % of taxes never reach you while the estates hold the purse.
burden.why: The catalogue's first constraint is a chronic shortage of money, with domains pledged widely and estates controlling taxation.
burden.shed_text: Pay off all your debt and learn Tax registers.

turned.name: Chamber in order
turned.text: Debt interest 30 % lower and a tenth more tax reaches you.

ambitions.name: Three crowns, one house
ambitions.hint: A boy, a stolen crown and two empty thrones.
ambitions.text: Rule Hungary and Bohemia, in personal union or by holding half their heartlands.

legacy.name: Danubian monarchy
legacy.text: Two more lords before strain, Foreign rule fades a quarter faster, prestige +1.

ambitions.name: The empty pockets filled
ambitions.hint: Every castle pawned is a castle lost.
ambitions.text: Have five more royal provinces than at the start.

legacy.name: Redeemed domains
legacy.text: Royal provinces pay 15 % more tax, debt interest 30 % lower, tax collectors 10 % stronger.

ambitions.name: The walls hold
ambitions.hint: Twice the tents will ring the city.
ambitions.text: Hold Vienna and half of central Hungary.

legacy.name: Bells of St Stephen
legacy.text: Garrisons 20 % stronger and bloodshed no longer angers the frontier.

ambitions.name: Lions of Trieste
ambitions.hint: A small port that Venice would rather see empty.
ambitions.text: Hold Trieste and keep at least ten war ships.

legacy.name: Trieste arsenal
legacy.text: Ships build 20 % faster and port provinces raise 20 % more sailors.

ambitions.name: The hawk's castle
ambitions.hint: The house is named for a castle its heirs no longer hold.
ambitions.text: Win back Habsburg castle in the Aargau from the Swiss.

legacy.name: Pikes of the hawk
legacy.text: Commanders may fight in Gewalthaufen, and hired companies cost a fifth less.

ambitions.name: The chancery reformed
ambitions.hint: Estates grant; ministers count.
ambitions.text: Know Professional bureaucracy and keep at least ten schools.

legacy.name: United chancery
legacy.text: Two more officials before strain, officials reach full effect a year sooner, tax reach +4 %.

classification.entity_type_notes: Group record for autonomous Igbo village groups governed by elders, title societies and assemblies.

geography.extent_1444: Igboland east and west of the Niger.
advantages: Familiar terrain and dispersed settlement hard to conquer

trade_routes: Regional markets

identity.background: Densely settled village groups with assemblies, age grades and title societies; Nri ritual influence and Aro networks (later).

geography.extent_1444: City of Genoa and the Ligurian Riviere (di Ponente and di Levante), from near Ventimiglia to near Sarzana; claims on Corsica; overseas colonies separately catalogued.
geography.climate_terrain_resources: Narrow coastal strip backed by mountains; little arable land.

trade_routes: Western Mediterranean to Iberia, Flanders, England
Levant and Black Sea via colonies
Lombard hinterland

economy.resource_base: Capital and shipping; Ligurian olive oil and wine.

society.settlement_pattern: Dense port city; small coastal towns.

identity.background: Genoa was Venice's great maritime rival with colonies in the Aegean and Black Sea, but was politically unstable: the "popular" doges came from rival clans (Adorno, Campofregoso/Fregoso) supported by noble alberghi (Doria, Spinola, Fieschi, Grimaldi) and outside powers. The 1435 victory over Alfonso at Ponza was followed by revolt against Milan. In 1444 the Adorno held the dogeship and made peace with Alfonso.

possible_future_paths.historical_outcome: Charles VII took lordship 1458; Milanese lordship 1464.
Bank of San Giorgio took Corsica 1453.

capital.name: No single capital; Barcelona, Zaragoza and Valencia are the realm capitals, and the king resided in Naples

geography.extent_1444: The royal domain (Île-de-France, Champagne, Berry, Touraine, Poitou, Languedoc, Lyonnais, Auvergne under Bourbon, Picardy south of the Somme towns) and the great fiefs. English hold Normandy, Maine and Guyenne (Bordeaux-Bayonne) plus Calais.
geography.core_region: Loire valley and Paris basin (court mostly in Touraine and Berry)
geography.climate_terrain_resources: Temperate fertile plains, vineyards, salt marshes; very large agricultural base.

capital.name: Paris (Parlement and administration); royal court at Tours, Bourges, Chinon, Loches

trade_routes: Mediterranean trade via Montpellier and Aigues-Mortes (Levant galleys of Jacques Cœur)
Lyon fairs
Atlantic salt and wine

economy.resource_base: Large fertile base recovering from war.

identity.background: The most populous kingdom of western Europe, devastated by the Hundred Years War and the Armagnac-Burgundian civil war, was recovering under Charles VII. Since the Treaty of Arras (1435) with Burgundy and the recovery of Paris (1436), the crown had suppressed the princes' revolt of 1440 (Praguerie), gained regular taxation (taille, aides) without consulting the Estates General, and in 1444 secured a truce with England. The écorcheurs, unemployed soldiery, were the chief domestic problem; the king sent them east in 1444 against the Swiss and Metz.

trade_routes: Coastal trade
Kilwa
Mombasa

identity.background: Island towns with mosques and small ruling houses (Mwinyi Mkuu tradition in Unguja is later formalised).

geography.extent_1444: Mainland Portugal and the Algarve; Ceuta in Morocco (recorded as portuguese_ceuta in af_north_sahara); Madeira and Porto Santo; Azores in early settlement; seasonal presence on the Saharan coast (Arguin).
geography.core_region: Lisbon and the Tagus estuary, Coimbra, Porto and the Entre-Douro-e-Minho
geography.climate_terrain_resources: Atlantic coastline with good harbours; mountainous north, Mediterranean-type south; salt, wine, olive oil, fish, cork; limited grain.
advantages: Long Atlantic coastline and maritime expertise

passes_and_corridors: Land frontier with Castile (Minho, Beira, Alentejo)
trade_routes: Atlantic coastal trade to Flanders and England
Mediterranean via Italian merchants
Atlantic islands
Saharan-Guinea coast (gold, slaves, gum)

economy.resource_base: Coastline, salt pans, vineyards, cork oak; Madeira timber and later sugar.
goods: Gold dust and enslaved people from the African coast (from the 1440s)

society.settlement_pattern: Coastal towns and dense rural north; thinly settled Alentejo.

identity.background: A compact Atlantic kingdom whose Avis dynasty, founded in the 1383-1385 crisis with English support, turned to overseas expansion: Ceuta (1415), the colonisation of Madeira and the Azores, and voyages down the African coast sponsored by Prince Henry. The failed attack on Tangier (1437) and the regency struggle after King Duarte's death made the 1440s politically delicate, but the regent Pedro, an internationally travelled prince, governed effectively and allowed Henry's ventures to accelerate.

possible_future_paths.path: Civil war between regent and nobility
prerequisites: Afonso V comes of age under Braganza influence

possible_future_paths.path: Atlantic slave trade and Guinea trade
possible_future_paths.historical_outcome: Arguin post built in the late 1440s-1450s; slave trade grew; transatlantic trade later.

prerequisites: Royal resources and noble desire for war

names.common_en: Morocco (Marinid sultanate under the Wattasid regency)

capital.name: Fez (Fas al-Jadid palace-city and Fas al-Bali)
No fixed capital; itinerant court (Valladolid, Madrigal, Tordesillas, Medina del Campo most frequent)
Dijon (ducal capital of the duchy); the court resided mostly at Brussels, Lille, Bruges and Hesdin
capital.notes: There was no single capital; the itinerant court increasingly favoured Brussels in the 1440s.

capital.name: No fixed capital; Edinburgh, Stirling and Perth
capital.notes: Edinburgh Castle and Stirling were key to controlling the king.

classification.entity_type_notes: Centralised bureaucratic monarchy under an emperor claiming the Mandate of Heaven, governing through civil-service ministries, provinces and a hereditary military-household (weisuo) system.

geography.extent_1444: China proper (the two metropolitan areas and thirteen provinces) from Liaodong to Yunnan and from Gansu to the coast, including Hainan. Guard-system outposts and nominal guards beyond the frontier in Manchuria and west of Jiayu Pass; the steppe north of the garrison line was not held.
geography.core_region: North China plain (Beijing) and the lower Yangzi (Jiangnan) economic heartland, linked by the Grand Canal.
geography.climate_terrain_resources: Temperate north China plain (wheat, millet) and humid subtropical south (rice); mountainous southwest with silver and copper mines in Yunnan; silk, cotton and porcelain production in Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

capital.name: Beijing (Shuntian)
capital.notes: Nanjing retained as auxiliary capital with a parallel ministry structure.

passes_and_corridors: Juyong Pass and the Beijing northern passes
trade_routes: Grand Canal internal trade
Tribute-horse trade at frontier markets with Mongols and Jurchens
Tea-horse trade with Tibet via Sichuan and Shaanxi
Tribute missions from Central Asia via Hami
Official maritime tribute routes to Ryukyu, Southeast Asia and Japan

economy.resource_base: The largest agrarian economy of its time, with highly productive rice agriculture in the south.

society.settlement_pattern: Dense rural settlement with large cities (Beijing, Nanjing, Suzhou, Hangzhou); military garrisons along frontiers; sparse Han settlement in the southwest.

identity.background: Founded on the ruins of Yuan rule by Zhu Yuanzhang, the Ming built a strongly centralised state with the capital moved to Beijing by the Yongle Emperor (r.1402-1424), who also campaigned in Mongolia, occupied Annam and sent Zheng He's fleets across the Indian Ocean. Under the Hongxi and Xuande emperors (1424-1435) policy turned to retrenchment: Annam was abandoned (1427), the last great voyage sailed in 1431-1433, and frontier defence shifted towards a defensive garrison line. The Zhengtong Emperor came to the throne aged eight in 1435.

possible_future_paths.path: Tumu crisis: an imperial campaign against the Oirat ends in disaster and capture of the emperor
prerequisites: Favourite-led decision to campaign in person
blockers_or_alterations: A capable military leadership or avoiding a personal imperial campaign
possible_future_paths.historical_outcome: August/September 1449 the Zhengtong Emperor was captured at Tumu; Yu Qian defended Beijing; the Jingtai Emperor was enthroned and the captive returned in 1450.

possible_future_paths.path: Resume maritime expeditions or open private maritime trade
possible_future_paths.historical_outcome: Voyages were not resumed; private trade was legalised only in 1567 at Yuegang.

possible_future_paths.path: Consolidate the southwest by turning tusi into regular administration
possible_future_paths.historical_outcome: Gradual and partial; large-scale conversion came under the Qing.

capital.name: No fixed capital (mobile ordo)
capital.notes: Seasonal camps in western and central Mongolia.

capital.name: Hanseong (Hanyang, modern Seoul)
capital.notes: Capital since 1394 (with a brief return to Gaegyeong 1399-1405).

classification.entity_type_notes: Elective-within-a-royal-lineage kingship over appointed and hereditary provincial lords, centred on a royal town.

geography.extent_1444: Roughly the plateau and valleys between the lower Congo river and the Loje/Dande in the south, and from the Atlantic coast (Soyo) east towards the Kwango; exact limits in the 1440s are unknown.
geography.climate_terrain_resources: Savanna plateau with gallery forest, two rainy seasons; millet, sorghum, yams, bananas and palm products; raffia cloth, salt on the coast, copper deposits to the north and south.
advantages: Control of shell currency and salt
Densest population in the region around the capital

passes_and_corridors: Routes east to Malebo Pool and the Kwango
trade_routes: Salt and shells from the coast inland
Copper from the north (Mindouli) and the Bembe area
Cloth (raffia) exchange with the Kwango and Tio

economy.resource_base: Plateau agriculture, palm and raffia, coastal salt, nearby copper.

society.settlement_pattern: Royal and provincial towns (mbanza) surrounded by dispersed villages.

identity.background: Kikongo-speaking kingdom founded, according to traditions recorded from the 16th century, when Lukeni lua Nimi crossed from Vungu north of the Congo and conquered the Mpemba Kasi/Mbanza Kongo area, allying with the Nsaku Lau lineage of Mbata. Kingship passed among descendants of the founder chosen by electors, and the king appointed provincial governors who collected tribute in cloth, food and nzimbu shell currency.

possible_future_paths.path: Contact with Portuguese navigators and royal conversion
prerequisites: Portuguese voyages reach the Congo mouth
possible_future_paths.historical_outcome: Diogo Cão reached the Congo in 1483; Nzinga a Nkuwu was baptised in 1491 and Afonso I built a Kongolese Catholic church.
Kongo claimed "Angola" in royal titles by 1535, but Ndongo became independent and hostile in the 16th century.
Disputed successions recurred (1506-1509, 1560s-1570s) and after Mbwila (1665) the kingdom split for decades.

capital.name: Royal residence on the plateaux (Mbe in later times)
